system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## 0. The "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have not relied on that, and I recommend you don't either.** It is the counterparty's characterisation in its own draft. Nearly every position it labels [STANDARD] is seller-favourable and departs from the baseline (debt-free/cash-free, 100% clean title).

**Action:** Confirm internally whether any of these points were actually agreed, such as in a term sheet or call notes. Unless they were, reply that **all positions remain open**. Ask that the labels be removed so they can't later be cited as evidence of agreement.

---

## 1. Structural issues: together, these hollow out the warranty protection

The most dangerous items are not individual numbers. The danger is how four provisions stack together:

| Seller provision | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2: General disclosure** of the whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Anything anywhere in the data room or a public register qualifies every warranty |
| **Cl 8.3: Buyer knowledge**, including advisers' knowledge and anything "discoverable" | A second, broader bar on the same ground, extended to constructive knowledge |
| **Cl 12.3/13: All limitations apply to all Claims** "unless expressly stated otherwise" | Caps, thresholds and time limits silently apply to indemnities, tax, title, leakage and price adjustments |
| **Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5: Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance** apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Purports to reach fraud and misleading conduct |

Taken together, we would be paying AUD 24m with warranties that respond to almost nothing.

**Push back:**
- **Disclosure:** Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. If any data room disclosure is conceded, limit it to a defined, indexed, USB-archived set of documents. Strike "public registers" and "publicly searchable records" except for specified searches on a specified date. Disclosure must not qualify title/capacity warranties, the tax indemnity, or any specific indemnity.
- **Buyer knowledge (8.3):** Delete it. As a fallback, limit it to the *actual* knowledge of named individuals on the Wattlebridge deal team, of a matter they knew constituted a breach. No adviser or constructive ("discoverable") knowledge. It must never apply to specific indemnities, which exist precisely because we know about the issue.
- **Default rule (cl 13):** Reverse it. Limitations apply **only to general Warranty Claims** unless expressly extended.
- **Carve-outs from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance:** fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its personnel; title/capacity; tax; specific indemnities; leakage and price adjustment. Note that a contractual non-reliance clause will not exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s 18. It can still affect the reliance analysis, so the fraud carve-out should be express.

---

## 2. Limitation package (cl 12)

**Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency).** The Seller proposes the 20% cap and 18-month window "for administrative simplicity." **Reject.** If title fails, we have lost the whole AUD 24m. Market position is a cap at **100% of the price**, no de minimis or basket, and a long claims period. That means at least the contractual limitation period under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW), which is 6 years, or 12 if the SPA is executed as a deed. Many buyers seek 7 years.

**Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." **Reject.**
- **Tax:** Seek a standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, capped at the price, with a claims period of about 5–7 years to track ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods. It should expressly cover payroll tax, PAYG and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses.
- **IP:** IP is likely core value in an analytics business. At minimum, apply an elevated cap and a longer period to IP warranties, and give Ironquay its own indemnity (see §3.4).

**General cap: 20% (AUD 4.8m).** This is within the range seen in Australian mid-market deals, so it is not the hill to die on. The right figure depends on whether we are taking **W&I insurance**. If we are, a low seller cap may be acceptable provided the uninsurable known risks (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) sit in specific indemnities outside the cap. If there is no W&I, push for 30–50%.

**Thresholds.**
- De minimis AUD 25k (~0.1%): seek AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
- Basket AUD 250k (~1%) on an excess-only basis: seek **tipping (first-dollar)** recovery once the basket is reached, and/or a basket of ~0.5% (AUD 120k).

**Time limit: 18 months.** This is common. I'd seek **24 months**, or at least enough to cover a full audit cycle after Completion. Confirm the Completion date against the 30 June year-end.

---

## 3. Specific known issues: these need conditions, completion mechanics, price or indemnities, not warranties

Every item in this section is specifically disclosed, so warranties will not protect us. Each must be dealt with expressly.

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (DD-002): ~AUD 3.6m revenue, ~30% of FY26
The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." DL 2 confirms that no final consent exists and that the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be satisfied.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit**, waivable only by the Buyer. It is satisfied only on delivery of an **unconditional written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, acting reasonably**, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
- Raise the Seller's obligation to "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours."
- Require Buyer participation in, and approval of, any consent terms. If Bluefen extracts concessions such as pricing, term changes or guarantees, the Buyer must agree to them.
- Include a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.
- Consider a price adjustment or earn-out protection if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces volume within 12 months after Completion.
- **DD task:** Review the cl 11.3 conditions now. They may impose obligations on the Buyer group.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (DD-003): ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
"Release to be provided following Completion" is **inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline**. It also exposes the Company to a change-of-control event of default under cl 8.1 at the moment we acquire it.

**Push back:**
- Riverlark debt is **Debt** and must be repaid **at Completion out of the price**, under a payoff letter specifying the exact payout figure and per diem.
- Completion deliverables:
  - signed deed of release
  - PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them within a set short period)
  - discharge of any real property security
  - release of any Company guarantees given for Seller group debt
- Funds flow: the payout goes directly to Riverlark, and the Seller receives the net amount.

### 3.3 Completion bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" yet omits them from the funds flow. The **Company is the employer** and will bear the legal liability. The bonuses also attract PAYG withholding, likely payroll tax, and potentially superannuation guarantee, depending on whether they are ordinary time earnings.

**Push back:**
- Treat bonuses **plus all on-costs** as Transaction Costs/Debt deducted from the price.
- Alternatively, have the Seller fund them through the Company's payroll at Completion, itemised in the funds flow.
- Add an indemnity for any shortfall, including amounts paid after Completion where continued-employment conditions are met later.
- Check whether any bonus is payable to a key person we need to retain. Payment at Completion may weaken retention, so consider deferring part of it under Buyer-designed arrangements.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (DD-004 cl 7.3 / DD-010)
Title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. AUD 180k appears open. On the documents, **the Company may not own those materials.** An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" does not address that.

**Push back:**
- Require the Seller to pay or procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion, with evidence of cleared funds. Alternatively, deduct or escrow the amount.
- Completion deliverable: a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay, including moral rights consents where relevant.
- The indemnity should cover all Losses from any defect in the Company's title to or right to use SOW3 materials. That includes third-party claims, injunctions, and re-development or replacement costs. It should sit **outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure**, with a longer claims period.
- **DD task:** Confirm how central SOW3 materials are to the product.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006): ~1,240 records
The Seller calls this a "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter is more candid: access, scope and notifiability are **unresolved** as of 22 September.

Turnover appears to be ~AUD 12m (Bluefen's ~AUD 3.6m is ~30%), so the Company is very likely outside the small-business exemption and subject to the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme**. Where there are reasonable grounds to suspect an eligible data breach, an assessment must be completed within 30 days (s 26WH). The incident appears to be at least six weeks old. Whether that window has been met is a live question, and any non-compliance is itself a potential exposure. Penalties under the Privacy Act were significantly increased in 2022.

**Push back:**
- **Pre-Completion covenants:**
  - complete the eligible data breach assessment promptly
  - make any required OAIC and individual notifications
  - give the Buyer the incident timeline, the forensic findings and the assessment, with Buyer consultation rights on any regulator correspondence
- **Specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties (to the extent lawfully indemnifiable), investigation and notification costs, third-party and customer claims (including any Bluefen fallout), and remediation. It must sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure.
- Consider a retention or escrow until the regulatory position is closed.
- Consider a Buyer walk right if a material regulatory investigation commences before Completion.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008/DD-011): 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k
The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs." The DL itself flags that they are related and should be "read together for timing/scope," and says nothing about whether they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued. Three identical contracts just under a round figure is a pattern worth testing. They may have been split to fall below a board-approval or conduct-of-business threshold.

**Push back / DD:**
- Obtain all three contracts, their dates, approvals and term/termination provisions.
- Check them against the SPA conduct-of-business covenants. If they were entered after the locked-box or signing date without consent, they are a covenant breach.
- If they are prepaid but unearned, or are long-term commitments not reflected in working capital, treat them as Debt or leakage, or require termination at Seller cost.
- Confirm that Sandbar is not a Seller-related party. If it is, treat the payments as leakage.

### 3.7 Title (DD-012)
A share register entry alone is **not** sufficient evidence of title.

**Require:**
- an uncapped fundamental title warranty (see §2)
- an ASIC company extract reconciling with the register
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company showing no security over the shares
- confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP entitlements or shareholder agreements
- waiver of any constitutional pre-emptive rights
- original or replacement share certificates and executed transfers at Completion

### 3.8 Lower-priority items
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Make giving the notification a Completion deliverable or a Seller covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Seller says no consent is triggered. Have counsel confirm there is no change-of-control or "deemed assignment" language elsewhere in the contract.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** Generally acceptable. Make sure it cannot be used to argue that a disclosed matter is not a breach for indemnity purposes.
- **Staleness:** The DL is dated 22 September 2026, six weeks ago. Require an updated Disclosure Letter. Any disclosure against warranties repeated at Completion should be limited to matters arising after signing, outside the Seller's control, and should give the Buyer a walk right if material.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| Priority | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | "[STANDARD] / already agreed" framing | Reject. All points open unless we have a record of agreement |
| **Critical** | General disclosure + buyer-knowledge bar | Specific "fairly disclosed" only; delete 8.3 or limit to actual knowledge of named individuals |
| **Critical** | Limitations apply to all Claims; non-reliance | Limitations apply to general warranties only; carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, leakage |
| **Critical** | Title/capacity under general cap | 100% price cap, no thresholds, 6–7 years |
| **Critical** | Riverlark AUD 3.2m post-Completion release | Repay at Completion from price; payoff letter, deed of release, PPSR releases |
| **Critical** | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Buyer-only CP, unconditional consent satisfactory to Buyer, all reasonable endeavours, long-stop/walk right |
| **High** | Ironquay SOW3 title | Pay or escrow AUD 180k; confirmatory assignment at Completion; full IP indemnity outside limits |
| **High** | DD-006 privacy incident | NDB assessment and notification covenants, information rights, uncapped specific indemnity, retention |
| **High** | Bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | Deduct as Transaction Costs including payroll tax, super and PAYG; show in funds flow; indemnity |
| **High** | Tax / IP under general regime | Standalone tax indemnity (5–7 years, price cap); enhanced IP protection |
| **Medium** | Sandbar AUD 330k | Full DD; test against conduct covenants and related-party/leakage rules; treat as Debt if appropriate |
| **Medium** | Cap 20%, de minimis 25k, basket 250k excess, 18 months | Depends on W&I. Seek tipping basket, lower thresholds, 24 months, higher cap if no W&I |
| **Low** | Lease notice, Mossvale, stale DL | Completion deliverables; confirm no CoC trigger; updated DL |

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Confirm the W&I decision, since it drives the cap and threshold strategy.
2. Send a short cover note rejecting the "pre-agreed" framing before issuing the mark-up.
3. Commission the targeted DD follow-ups: Bluefen cl 11.3, the DD-006 timeline and assessment, the Sandbar contracts, the SOW3 materials, and title searches.
4. Prepare the mark-up with a specific indemnities schedule covering Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Bluefen and tax, plus the funds-flow corrections.

This is a first-pass issues review for the deal team. Positions should be confirmed by the supervising NSW-qualified lawyers before they go to the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
